consumer_binding.selector: registered principal-scoped operation DTO and proof carriers

schemas.description: Closed holder-signed Contact scope replacement payload, including the peer XOR, stable basis, version, predecessor and full granted-scope set.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form ak:<kind>:<uuid> unless a special form below applies.

Storage implementations MAY store raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ak:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The UUID segment MUST be RFC 9562 UUID version 7 (48-bit Unix-millisecond timestamp + 4-bit version=7 + 12-bit rand_a + 2-bit variant=10b + 62-bit rand_b), serialized as the canonical 36-character lowercase hex form `xxxxxxxx-xxxx-7xxx-Nxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` where N ∈ {8,9,a,b}.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference using an active digest-suite id (v1: sha256 or profile-gated blake3); distinct from ak:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Realm-scoped pseudonymous credential reference; validated by the E2EE profile. v1 core uses Realm as the boundary; Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque install-plan token; do not parse it as UUIDv7.
special_forms.description: Applet install-plan identifier. The suffix is an opaque non-empty base64url token.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte receipt-claims digest or the complete typed content-addressed identifier.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed ServiceRegistrationReceipt identifier derived from canonical receipt claims.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte delegation digest or the complete typed content-addressed reference.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed membership-compensation delegation reference. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal the SHA-256 delegation_digest derived from the profile-defined digest-free canonical core.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as a content-addressed canonical Seal hash.
Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.
special_forms.description: Canonical protocol cell identifier. The complete ak.component.<facet-path>.v<n> family identifier is embedded unchanged after ak:cell:. When the registry declares cell_subject: null for a family, the canonical subject segment is the literal ASCII string 'null' (ak:cell:<component>:null); the cell is located by the Event envelope realm_id and implementations MUST NOT encode realm_id, Realm role classification, or any payload-derived value into that segment. See spec/v1/zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the scope string as an opaque deployment-level identifier; it appears in server describe, Realm policy, and high-risk proof transcripts.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk proofs (e.g. ak.cross_signing.reset §14.1). NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

id_kinds.description: Moderation appeal ID — opaque key for the ak.component.moderation.appeal.v1 cell. Created by ak.moderation.appeal.submit; referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.
Audit Applet Binding ID. Created by ak.audit.applet_binding and referenced by audit session request/authorize/notice/release events.
Audit release session ID. Threads ak.audit.session.request, authorize, notice, release, and close events for one bounded historical audit window.
Audit release manifest ID. Created by ak.audit.release for a sealed historical release under an active audit binding/session.

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_kind). A pair MAY have multiple series during rotation or migration; the active series is selected by the signed active-series record, not by server return order. Used by ak.schema.key_backup.v1.series_id and recovery strands to detect rollback. See identity/key-management.md §7.6.
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form

SFU-local participant handle. Scope limited to `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`; derived from `(realm_id, call_id, focus_id, device_id, issuer_service_id, issued_at_bucket)` by the media service token issuer. MUST NOT carry any actor-identifying material; only appears in an `ak.call.state.roster_delta` join participant value and in `participant_binding`. The wire value MUST use the canonical UUIDv7-shaped `ak:rtc_participant:<uuid>` form; implementations MAY derive the random bits from the media-service token input, but the version and variant nibbles MUST satisfy the UUIDv7 pattern.
Abstract capability definition reference ID; signed grant objects use ak:grant:<uuid>.

Circle object ID — intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary. Hosts its own membership (strict subset of parent Realm.members), history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and optional independent MLS group. Does NOT carry federation identity, policy server, or capability registry — those remain on the parent Realm. See zh/models/circle.md.
Agent Sidecar object ID — controller-owned private AI workspace, singleton per (realm_id, controller_id), with derived eligible-Agent access. See zh/models/sidecar.md.
Consent grant/revoke/request identifier shared by Arkret consent events and MIMI interop DTOs.

Device identifier (ak:device:<uuid>). A device is a typed ID scoped to an owning principal, NOT a DID and NOT an actor principal. Device keys are registered as verification methods under the owning principal DID via ak.device.authorize.
Signed capability grant object ID used by ak.schema.capability.v1 and grant/revoke references.

Non-secret Principal Server administrative ID for one account-owned online invite locator. The ID is exposed only on the authenticated self management surface and is distinct from the opaque bearer locator_token.
Transient Signal Message preview stream instance ID; never a durable object or Event identity
Opaque identifier for a durable or reserved multi-phase protocol operation instance.

Stable session identifier bound by every proof transcript, backup decrypt proof and MLS Welcome replay during one recovery strand. Referenced by ak.schema.recovery_receipt.v1 and by §15 recovery proofs. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §15.

Space object ID — structural grouping object inside a Realm (board, list, swimlane, calendar bucket, etc.). Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership / policy / E2EE group; resolves to the containing Realm.
Realm object ID — security / sync / auth / E2EE boundary. Always carries membership, policy, history_visibility, MLS group binding, and federation policy.
id_kinds.id_form_note: Collaboration Realms are event-derived (UUIDv8, encoding.md section 4.0). Principal Control Realms are subject-derived from the principal DID (H("ak:realm:principal-control:v1:" || did), UUIDv7 layout) so the address stays computable from the DID alone; their identity anchor is did_inception, not the genesis Event. Neither form is producer-chosen and the branch is fixed by the create's purpose.

id_kinds.description: Durable RecoveryTransaction, SecurityRotationTransaction, federation, or applet transaction identifier.

Reserved UUIDv7 identity of the Principal Server signed, RecoveryTransaction-bound one-time Account Authority ticket. The id is fixed at transaction create; signed ticket bytes are issued only after the transaction is durable.

id_kind_registry.uuid_form_rules: Every typed ak:<kind>:<uuid> uses exactly one of two constructions, declared per kind by id_form. producer_allocated = RFC 9562 UUIDv7, assigned by the service or client that mints the identifier. event_derived = RFC 9562 UUIDv8 with the content-bound layout of zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4.0: 34-bit second timestamp derived from created_at plus 88 bits taken from the leftmost 11 octets of the creating Event's event_digest. An event_derived id has no producer-chosen bits, so forging one that collides with an existing object requires 2^88 hash operations instead of typing a string. Implementations MUST NOT choose the form per site; it is fixed by this registry.

operation_registry.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise supported_operations and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see surface_classes); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.
surface_classes defines the closed tier vocabulary and surface_groups is the sole canonical operation grouping view; generators MUST NOT emit a third top-level surfaces collection.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>. The kind segment MUST be one of read, query, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name. read is the canonical safe/idempotent computation kind for surfaces bound to HTTP QUERY; query remains valid for operation families not yet migrated.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex query body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (read/query/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

Every write operation MUST declare durable_effect. kind=event_log identifies an Arkret Event committed by successful completion and declares either event_kinds[] or an event_kind_source JSON path; kind=actor_private_event declares the actor-private Event kind committed; kind=none declares no Arkret Event and requires a stable rationale. Service-local durable state, identity-method logs, queues, session/material stores, external effects and returned-but-uncommitted Event material all use kind=none with an accurate rationale. Missing, unknown or inactive declared Event kinds fail closed.

Every operation MUST declare body_class, a closed value of non_streaming_json, streaming_ndjson, or binary_stream. body_class=non_streaming_json binds the operation to the general size contract in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2.1: canonical request/response body <= 8 MiB, HTTP message content wire bytes <= 16 MiB, Content-Encoding MUST be absent, and every byte overflow maps to payload_too_large. streaming_ndjson and binary_stream operations are excluded from the whole-body limits and MUST define their own per-frame / per-chunk / pending bounds (scalability-constraints section 2.1.7).

max_canonical_body_bytes is OPTIONAL and only for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose normative limit is LOWER than the general 8 MiB. It MUST NOT declare a value above 8 MiB, and deployments MUST NOT lower the general interoperability constants through Describe (scalability-constraints section 2.1.6).

max_items is REQUIRED for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose request or response carries a top-level array with a normative count bound. max_items and the byte budget are a conjunctive two-dimensional constraint: a count bound never promises that max_items objects of near-maximum size fit in one body, and implementations MUST NOT lower a registered count because a fixture-median product exceeds the byte budget (scalability-constraints section 2.1.5).

surface_classes.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Arkret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
surface_classes.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
surface_classes.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
surface_classes.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

operations.notes: Account Authority exchanges an OIDC authorization code for an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, register, and issue_session_grant. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy state and atomically acquires, renews, or fences an identity-creation lease for the authenticated service account. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. A different holder cannot take an unexpired lease; after expiry, a newly authenticated holder for the same service account may fence it and must preserve any reserved principal_id, operation digest, and public DID-operation checkpoint.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id and its canonical operation digest, persists the public operation checkpoint, renews the same-holder lease, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, principal_id, operation digest, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh inception the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] from the operation itself (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod) and requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, and writes the service-account binding. The (account, principal_id, operation_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

Authorizes a sibling device after the verified current device confirms the SAS/QR transcript. When device_pairing_request_id is present, the Account Authority MUST atomically require and consume the unexpired pending staged record whose pairing_code and new_device_pubkey exactly match the request, and MUST verify challenge_proof by recomputing the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 transcript from that staged record (device-lifecycle.md section 2.1.2); a mismatch or a failing signature performs no device authorization. A byte-equality comparison of the proof is NOT sufficient.

Managed-DID (account-authority) device enrollment, device-lifecycle.md §5.4 / key-management.md §5.0.6. The authenticated session asks its designated enrollment authority to mint a service_attested ak.device.authorize for this session's own device; the authority signs with its persistent enrollment key (never the principal SSK) and returns the full Event. The caller submits it verbatim to POST /_arkret/self/events. Distinct from pair_device (§2.1), which lands an existing-device SAS/QR approval and carries a pairing_code; enroll_device is only the bootstrap / first-device path where no sibling device can approve. The authority MUST require actor_seq=1, a verified identity-creation binding receipt for the same principal/account, and no existing active device; a bare session grant or actor_seq>1 MUST NOT enroll a second long-term device. Later devices use pair_device or the recovery re-anchor strand.

Cancels exactly one pending founding or sibling bootstrap transaction under its closed device_bootstrap bearer plus DPoP. The durable ledger key is (transaction_id,idempotency_key); byte-identical retries return the first closed outcome, different bytes conflict, explicit accepted cancellation alone yields cancelled, the independent transaction deadline alone yields expired, and every other failure remains pending/retryable. This operation never mints a replacement Event or standard credential.

Enrollment-authority B-model recovery only. Consumes a Principal Server signed RecoveryAuthorityTicket bound to one durable RecoveryTransaction and the complete authorization preimage, including the closed authorize Event publication intent and its CBA proof bundles. The Account Authority revalidates ticket signature/audience/TTL/current delegation, every transaction/plan/device/generation/DID/Event/basis/authority-set binding and the replacement device possession proof, then durably stores and returns one byte-stable outcome containing the authority-signed ak.device.authorize Event, the matching authority-signed publication lease, and the exact CBA proof bundles. Same ticket_id plus identical canonical request returns the recorded outcome; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict. It is not founding enroll_device and cannot authorize an unbound session.

Account Authority single-call session-grant exchange. The response is the client-visible SessionGrantOutcome; any Principal-side local session provisioning is internal. There is no separate client-visible grant-to-bearer exchange step: the client presents ak.session.grant directly to /_arkret/self/* with DPoP (api-conventions §3.3). For proof_kind=oidc_code_exchange, the Account Authority exchanges the authorization code and validates issuer/state/nonce/redirect_uri/principal/device/audience binding. For proof_kind=pre_registration_handoff, the caller instead presents Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP; the handoff's service account MUST already be bound to the requested principal_id. principal_id is required for every proof kind and MUST already have a verified account binding; unknown or unbound returns principal_unknown (404). The Account Authority MUST NOT derive or mint a principal DID from OIDC. A first OIDC interaction may create only the account handoff; the client completes cold-root custody and canonical register before requesting a session grant. For proof_kind=agent_key_proof when high-risk scope needs controller approval, the endpoint returns 403 ErrorEnvelope with error.code=claim_required and closed agent_human_approval_error_details; it never returns CAPTCHA, OTP, password, or browser challenge material to the runtime.

DPoP-bound session-grant rotation (account-lifecycle §4.1, device-lifecycle §3.3). An authorized device presents a DPoP holder proof for the grant's cnf.jkt plus a fresh DID/device proof bound to principal_id, device_id, audience, request_canonical_digest, challenge, issued_at, and expires_at; expires_at - issued_at MUST be <=300s. The old grant is single-use revoked. Account Authority-local op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Explicitly rotates a restricted recovery grant into a normal replacement-device grant after the bound RecoveryTransaction is completed. Requires the old grant DPoP holder proof, terminal device-attested receipt, accepted device authorization projection and current model generation. The old grant is consumed and never widened in place. Same transaction_id plus old_grant_id and identical canonical request returns the recorded promotion; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ak.gate.account.command.logout request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ak.session.grant and terminate that session's grant rotation chain. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ak.gate.account.command.logout. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Principal Server validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether it is active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Principal Server can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The handler validates the current ak.session.grant + DPoP, terminates the Auth-side auth session / grant rotation chain through ak.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Final native Agent runtime-key authorization. The closed Ed25519 possession proof MUST be byte-identical to the current persisted runtime request and still fresh; the authority rebuilds its server-record-bound transcript, stable runtime binding and ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1 (including current proof digest) before accepting the controller-signed authorize Event. A stale prompt or any body/record/evidence mismatch fails closed without consuming the pairing handle.

Prepare fixes the new|existing branch, every reducer-derived coordinate, Event ID, canonical unsigned Event bytes and digest. It returns two controller-signing drafts for a new Sidecar and only an attach draft for an existing Sidecar. Commit accepts only proofs appended to those exact drafts. First ensure atomically admits exactly [ak.sidecar.create, ak.sidecar.context.attach]; attach must reference the reserved create Event with role after. The parent-Realm bootstrap exception is scoped only to create.

Controller-only dedicated Sidecar read surface. Returns the typed Sidecar plus desired/effective Agent access and reconciliation readiness. Unauthorized, nonexistent, and foreign-controller IDs use one indistinguishable not_found envelope. The backing Circle is included only as the Sidecar object's reducer-managed security binding and never as an ordinary Circle resource.

Controller-only paginated Sidecar list, optionally filtered by realm_id. Returns only Sidecars owned by the authenticated controller and never ordinary Circles or another controller's existence stubs.

Controller-only full replacement of one Account-Authority-owned per-scope selection. The authenticated bearer+DPoP session is the authority proof. First write uses expected_version=0; each accepted write increments the exact agent/scope slot by one. Governance ceilings and ordinary Agent capabilities are evaluated at action time and are not copied into this record.

Optional Account Authority browser redirect landing / handoff for deployments that use an OIDC redirect URI under /_arkret/gate/account. It MUST NOT issue or return SessionGrantOutcome, ak.session.grant, or Principal local session material; client-visible grant issuance remains ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.

source_signature_anchor.node_to_applet: Source-Service-ID current service DID verification method; Destination-Service-ID MUST equal the Applet registration service_id.
source_signature_anchor.applet_to_arkret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; DID part MUST equal Source-Service-ID and the active effective install service_id.

operations.notes: Issues a short-TTL, single-blob, read-only pre-signed URL whose authorization material rides in the URL itself (query string). Used as a deliberate carve-out of the no-credentials-in-URL rule (server-threat-model.md S21) so that browser primitives like /

Enqueues caller-supplied DeviceMessageEnvelope targets into recipient device queues. Each target carries a sender-assigned message_id copied unchanged into the stored envelope; the service deduplicates logical messages by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, message_id), returning the existing outcome for identical canonical target content and duplicate_conflict/message_id_conflict for different content. HTTP batch replay is additionally deduplicated by (sender, Idempotency-Key). Queue pruning is only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.

Explicit, cumulative, monotonic to-device delivery acknowledgement (client-sync.md §10.1). Queue deletion happens only here; stream cursor advancement (account subscribe after=, device_messages after=) is read-only and MUST NOT prune the queue. Re-acking the same or an older token is a legal no-op. Unknown / expired / cross-bound tokens are rejected with invalid_param (reason invalid_ack_token) without deleting anything.

Two-phase holder-local acceptance of one holder-signed ak.contact.requested fact. The accepted source receipt, peer closed XOR, full directional scope set and issuer-local slot lineage are durable replay inputs; no Private Consent Event is written or consulted.

Two-phase holder-local normal accept response. The service accepts only the holder-signed response Event bytes reserved for the current request slot, signs the matching normal-response acceptance receipt, and never writes Private Consent. Reject uses the separate ak.self.contact.command.reject operation. Glare is mechanically derived from two causally concurrent request receipts and forbids this operation.

Two-phase holder-local terminal reject. The service accepts only the holder-signed ak.contact.rejected Event bytes reserved for the exact current request slot, signs the matching rejection acceptance receipt, and provides durable exact replay/conflict semantics independently from normal accept responses.

Holder contact projection from source-signed request/response receipts, issuer-local Contact lineages and current signed head leases. Private Consent and account-data notes are never Contact authority.

Two-phase prepare/commit carrier for one holder-signed ak.contact.scope.update full-set directional replacement. Request/response establishes the issuer-local version 1 genesis; every scope replacement is version >= 2, exactly current+1, and references the exact issuer-local current head. Expansion and narrowing are both explicit signed replacements.
Holder-signed issuer-local lineage terminal. It consumes the Contact basis and generation; it does not carry scope replacement and does not write or revoke Private Consent.

Read the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. Returns the recommended default when no explicit override is stored; the response is never written into the target Realm durable event log.

Replace the authenticated subject's private invite-receive policy. The body MUST set subject_id equal to the session actor; the override shares the same store as ak.self.contact.command.tombstone(block_peer) denied_subjects writes.
Issues a fresh opaque locator for the authenticated principal. subject_id and recipient_service_id are server-derived; the raw bearer token is returned exactly once and MUST NOT be persisted.

Atomically revokes one authenticated-principal-owned locator and issues a new opaque token. The old token becomes indistinguishable from unknown tokens before success is returned. After an uncertain transport outcome, the client MUST first idempotently revoke the old locator_id and only then issue fresh material; directly issuing without that revocation can leave the old token active.
Idempotently revokes one locator owned by the authenticated principal. A same-principal retry returns the original revoked_at. Unknown, consumed, or cross-principal locator ids return not_found.

Query-only resolver for the pair's single stable Direct Conversation. It never creates: a Direct Conversation Realm is created solely by the founder derived from the pair's root Contact basis (normal branch takes the responder, glare branch takes the requests[0] issuer) through the direct_conversation_genesis admission variant of ak.realm.create. Outcomes are evaluated in a fixed order and expose creation_required, creation_blocked, awaiting_founder, provisional, found, suspended or temporarily_unavailable. Waiting never grants create authority to the non-founder and there is no timeout fallback or takeover.

Builds a ak.circle.create Operation in the named parent Realm and routes it through the local accept pipeline. Reducer-locked fields (mls_group_ref, state) MUST NOT be actor-supplied; encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor permits plaintext.
Lists Circles the caller may see within one parent Realm (required realm_id query). Directory visibility is enforced per Circle; non-members of a 'members'-visibility Circle MUST NOT see it.
Reads one Circle projection. Returns not_found when the Circle is invisible to the caller rather than disclosing existence.

Builds ak.circle.member.state. Activating another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to this Circle, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member (strict-subset invariant); a self-join is gated by join_rule.
Builds ak.circle.member.state with membership=leave for the path actor_id.

Rotates the Circle's bound MLS group. MUST NOT acknowledge a rotation without actually changing the cryptographic scope; returns unsupported_feature until the MLS genesis/commit/welcome cascade is wired end-to-end.
Builds ak.circle.archive; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_active).

Builds ak.circle.restore; transition follows the Circle lifecycle matrix (reducer rejects illegal transitions with circle_not_archived). Restore re-enables new writes after pending MLS membership removals are settled.
Builds ak.circle.tombstone (terminal). Response surfaces the terminal state with empty members.

Resource-side appeal against an operator takedown. The appeal packet MUST bind takedown_id, resource id, appellant DID, argument/evidence digest, requested_outcome and created_at, signed by the resource governance key or an authorized advocate; the Directory returns a signed decision receipt. See discovery-directory.md §8.7.

Return one bounded, manifest-committed chunk of a complete_control_state_v1 proof bundle for one authenticated, caller-visible Realm/scope. The request MUST name an exact locally trusted_anchor_seal_id and chunk_index; later chunks pin expected_bundle_digest. The service MUST build from that anchor and return mls_governance_anchor_unreachable instead of substituting another anchor. From one accepted Seal view it supplies enough complete state to rederive the closed key-access projection in mls-security-frontier-registry.json; callers cannot supply roots or choose frontier members. Responses bind canonical acquisition identity with proof_request_digest, commit all chunks under chunks_root, and use bundle_digest rather than accepted_seal_id as the logical content address. Each response is at most 4 MiB; the logical bundle is at most 256 MiB, 1024 chunks, 4096 Seals, 1048576 covered digests, 262144 control leaves and 128 frontier Events. Exceeding a total bound returns mls_governance_proof_bounds_exceeded with no partial output. Implementations MUST enforce Realm/scope visibility before materialization and MUST fail closed when any covered Event, control state, Seal path, chunk commitment, signature authority, or reducer profile cannot be reconstructed.

Canonical safe and idempotent Events range scan. HTTP uses RFC 10008 QUERY with JSON content. GET query-string and POST /query are compatibility bindings of this same operation and MUST NOT be advertised as independent operations.
Dereference a known set of event_id / event_digest references to full EventEnvelope objects. Point lookup by identifier, not a range scan — use ak.self.events.read.scan for selector-based reads.

Long-lived per-Realm / actor event stream with optional bounded catch-up replay. `dropped` and `resync_required` control frames MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms`, a server-directed minimum delay before opening another subscription for the same caller/selector scope; early reconnects are rejected with rate_limited / Retry-After.

Issue one immutable current-authority member receipt for a fully signed Control Move. Local device/Agent authorities use the same typed request and outcome without an HTTP hop. A caller canonically sorts distinct member receipts and may submit the resulting receipt set only when the current notary profile quorum and common-window rules are satisfied.

Read-only pre-admission of final signed Events followed by one authority-issued publication lease per Event. The operation never commits an Event or advances a frontier. Ordinary Events bind an accepted seal_ref/seal_basis; only complete registered genesis units may bind the ordered anchor_unit digest. Idempotent retry returns byte-identical leases.

Initial durable Event publication uses EventInitialSubmission: the signed Event remains the only business fact, while AuthorizationLease and optional CbaProofBundle values are independently verified publication evidence outside the Event digest. The ingress MUST persist and return the original IngressReceipt before lease expiry; byte-identical retry returns the stored receipt without changing received_at. For ak.invite.claim, the receiving Realm reducer remains the authoritative state machine and re-checks token commitment, allowlist, replay, proposal and expiry state.

Submit a client-signed Seal. Except for the canonical genesis exception, the signature MUST satisfy the predecessor governance state's ak.component.notary.v1 membership and threshold rules; Realm visibility or device ownership is insufficient. The receiver recomputes the Seal id, recursive coverage, completeness_root, state_root, signer authority and signature.
Federation peer Events surface describe. This endpoint describes the server-to-server peer event bindings; it is not a client self/events binding.

Federation peer frontier probe. Requires service-to-service authentication, Source/Destination service DID headers, trust-domain headers, and Realm federation_peer authorization. It returns the federation peer frontier response shape on the dedicated peer trust surface.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ak.self.events.read.scan, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

Read-only federation dependency resolution for canonical-bytewise sorted exact Event IDs, Event digests, and Seal refs in one Realm. Returns visible Events and receiver-relative CbaProofBundle values under a caller-selected response budget capped at 8 MiB. It never accepts an Event or Seal and never advances a frontier. Every selector is fully accounted for by a returned object or an indistinguishable same-type missing entry; if complete accounting cannot fit the budget, the whole operation returns limit_exceeded rather than a partial success.

Read-only service-authenticated retrieval of the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. The provider resolves the Event, verifies every echoed scope/group/epoch/ref/digest selector, hashes raw bytes against both explicit digests and content-addressed refs, and validates GroupInfo/tree consistency before returning an all-or-nothing response. It never returns private tree material, secrets, inferred leaf DTOs or proof-bundle leaves; consumers derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified RFC tree.

Federation peer Event publication. Each EventFederationSubmission carries the original signed Event. Ordinary online publication omits AuthorizationLease and uses an empty ingress_receipts array; explicit delayed/offline publication carries the lease and at least one original lease-bound IngressReceipt. An ak.member.state compensation publication additionally carries the unchanged transport-only membership_compensation_evidence and the receiver applies the same exact admission/incarnation/action/executor/single-use evaluator as initial submission. Request-level CbaProofBundle values provide receiver-relative dependency closure. The receiver independently validates every Event, optional lease, receipt threshold, compensation evidence, bundle object and reducer result. Ordinary missing dependencies use HTTP 200 partial items with reason_code=dependency_missing and non-empty typed missing sets; registered atomic units use top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with EventsDependencyMissingProblem and zero writes. A received response terminates that Idempotency-Key; a post-backfill submit uses a fresh key. The caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ak.invite.claim remains decided by the destination Realm reducer.

Read-only service-authenticated Account Authority query for the exact issuer actor-chain frontier and Principal Control Realm Seal frontier needed to sign one ak.account.status Event. The receiver verifies the signed authority_evidence, current issuer delegation and account/principal/PCR binding before disclosure. The response binds RealmActorFrontierView.actor_id to issuer_service_id and both frontier realm_id values to principal_control_realm_id; it grants no authority, accepts no Event and never synthesizes an empty PCR.

Account Authority or authorized Principal Server publication of exactly one ak.account.status Event into the account principal's Principal Control Realm. The caller uses service-to-service HTTP Message Signature authentication and a required Idempotency-Key covered by the signature. authority_evidence is Account Authority-signed transport evidence binding account_id, principal_id, principal_control_realm_id, issuer service and a live authority_ref; the receiver independently verifies it, the Event proof, exact Event/evidence field equality, current issuer key/delegation and PCR CBA closure. Initial publication carries the Event without an AuthorizationLease; downstream fanout adds receiver-signed account_status_receipts and CbaProofBundle values. AccountStatusReceipt proves local frontier acceptance, contains no AuthorizationLease id, and generic IngressReceipt is forbidden. Same key plus different canonical body is duplicate_conflict. A byte-identical retry returns the latest durable operation state, allowing pending_seal and fanout progress to converge without creating another Event. accepted or duplicate is terminal for the receiving server's frontier; multi-server propagation continues from a durable bounded outbox and never mutates the signed account-status payload.

Private Principal Server to Principal Server invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.recipient_service_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Unique closed XOR delivery carrier for original holder-signed Contact request, normal response, reject, scope replacement, or tombstone facts plus their exact source acceptance receipts and refreshable current proof. It never carries Direct Conversation binding or Realm Events. Branches use byte-identical durable replay; the receiver never re-signs or treats tentative/stale evidence as authority.

Atomic cross-Principal-Server KeyPackage claim. The destination KeyPackage authority is the sole CAS authority and MUST validate both the requester participant authorization and the outer source-service HTTP Message Signature. Idempotency is scoped by (Source-Service-ID, claim_request_id) and binds the canonical request digest; duplicate transport delivery returns the original outcome, but callers MUST use the query operation rather than replaying the command after an uncertain outcome. Success omits inventory counts and per-device failures.

Read-only recovery of the destination authority's durable peer-claim ledger after an uncertain command outcome. It requires the same authenticated source service and exact request_digest and returns only opaque claim state plus the original signed success outcome when one exists.
Federation peer snapshot manifest head for snapshot-assisted bootstrap. Requires service-to-service authentication and Realm federation_peer authorization.

Optional Signal Extension single-hop peer relay. The source batches original producer-signed encrypted SignalEnvelope values for one Realm and one destination service. The destination independently verifies peer authentication, current delivery binding, envelope proof, scope, Seal, signal_class, TTL and encrypted payload binding, then performs only local live fanout. The request MUST NOT carry Idempotency-Key; uncertain outcomes use drop_unconfirmed. The opaque accepted=true response reveals no Realm, scope, sender, recipient, binding, support, or per-signal result and is not a durable delivery receipt.

Encrypted-only Signal Extension send rail for ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1. Exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. It MUST NOT persist the envelope as a durable Event or advance actor_seq / Realm frontier.

Authenticated encrypted-only Signal Extension receive rail. Frames carry SignalEnvelope objects or bounded transport control frames; exact signal type and product target remain inside ciphertext. No catch-up or durable delivery guarantee.

Media service token exchange operation. Issues a short-lived (TTL <= 600s) backend_token + participant_binding for joining a focus declared in ak.realm.media_service.foci[]. Same wire across all backend types (livekit / mediasoup / janus / arkret_native); only backend_token shape is type-specific. Token issuer DID MUST be one of the Realm-authorized media service DIDs; clients reject otherwise (token_issuer_unauthorised). See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3.

The wrapper carries one complete DID method-native operation. did_method is the bare method discriminator and MUST equal the DID method component. Controller/update/recovery authorization comes only from the native operation; transport authentication is admission-only. Unsupported methods, generic replace/patch/document fallbacks, stale heads, and sibling forks fail closed. Exact canonical-operation retries are duplicate-success without a second history append.

Idempotently return or create the service DID bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base) registration key. The client supplies and controls a signed did:webvh inception operation; the Provider verifies the proof and endpoint binding and never receives private key material. Provider persistence MUST enforce UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base) and MUST reject an existing hosted document that declares the same key even when the mapping row is absent.
Read the service registration bound to the canonical (service_kind, public_base) key without creating or mutating identity state.

Issue a single-use control challenge for an external Organization DID. Two phases are mandatory: the registry issues and remembers the challenge, then the caller proves control against it. Folding the challenge into ensure would let the caller supply its own, at which point the receiver can establish neither freshness nor single use. The challenge binds purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, the requested scope set, the beneficiary local_admin_subject, and a window of at most 300 seconds, and MUST be consumed on first use. Binding the beneficiary here rather than only in the request is what stops a captured proof from being redirected: a proof that names only the organization and the version says nothing about who receives the scopes. Deliberately not idempotent: every call mints a fresh nonce, because reusing one challenge across attempts is exactly the replay window single use exists to close. A retry therefore yields a different challenge and the caller MUST prove against the newest one.

Establish the local binding for an external, already-published Organization DID, keyed on organization_id. The caller pins the resolved version_id and log_head_digest and proves control with a method-native proof whose kind is a closed two-member discriminator; creating a new Organization DID is a separate inception ceremony and has no member here. The control proof binds local_admin_subject, so a captured proof cannot be resubmitted naming a different beneficiary. Idempotency is per generation, not per organization: replaying the current generation's request returns created=false, while a request after revoke, or one that changes local_admin_subject or the scope set, opens registration_generation+1 with created=true. Without that generation the terminal revoked state and the organization-keyed idempotency would contradict each other. This operation registers a reference and a local administrative delegation only: it does not host the DID's method history, does not make this deployment the controller, and creates no Realm, membership, notary, capability or service delegation.

Read the local binding for one Organization DID without creating or mutating state; returns created=false. Only bindings the caller is authorised to manage or see are returned. A caller with no such authorisation MUST receive the same not-found answer as for an organization that was never registered, so the query cannot be used to enumerate which organizations a deployment has bound.

Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt, returning created=false. Scopes are not renegotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control the moment the organization rotates its controller, and because a first-time proof must not authorise the relationship indefinitely.

Withdraw the local binding, returning a receipt with status=revoked and created=false. Local act with local effect only: it does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history, which this deployment does not control. revoked is terminal; re-establishing the relationship requires a fresh ensure with a new challenge and proof.

Read the currently accepted ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 projection for the authenticated or explicitly selected principal. Returns active_policy=null when no accepted policy exists; does not publish, rotate, or revoke policy state.

Publish a signed ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1 genesis policy or rotation as a Principal Control Realm ak.policy.set EventInitialSubmission. The canonical Event payload is {policy_id,value}; value is the complete RecoveryPolicy, both policy ids MUST match, and state/reason MUST be absent. Event actor/scope, value.principal_id, lease and accepted control Seal MUST agree. The command returns success only after the Event is covered by the immutable acceptance_basis; before Seal materialization it returns retry-safe frontier_unavailable for the same Event id.

Issues the Principal Server signed one-time authority ticket only when the referenced enrollment-authority RecoveryTransaction is durable, its recovery session is verified and transaction-bound, prepared_plan_digest matches, and issue_authority_ticket is the current next_required_step. ticket_id was reserved by create. Same transaction/request/plan bytes return the stored ticket; different bytes return duplicate_conflict.

Creates exactly one durable RecoveryTransaction or SecurityRotationTransaction. The coordinator MUST atomically persist canonical request bytes, request_digest, the closed typed prepared_plan and prepared_plan_digest, all reserved public ids, and the initial resource before the first irreversible side effect. Recovery create also CAS-binds one already verified recovery session to this transaction. Same transaction_id plus identical bytes returns the recorded resource; different bytes returns duplicate_conflict.

Authoritative durable progress query by transaction_id. It MUST return the stored binding, accepted step prefix, next action, and terminal outcome and MUST NOT synthesize state from a short-lived HTTP idempotency cache.

Continues only the stored next_required_step. request_digest, prepared_plan_digest and expected_next_step MUST equal the resource; the endpoint is not a generic step or Saga executor. Client attestation is required only for issue_terminal_receipt or local_commit and must bind transaction/request/plan plus the pre-reserved output_ref. When all coordinator-owned recovery steps are accepted but the device is offline, the resource remains awaiting_device_attestation rather than completed.

Issues the durable, single-use, short-TTL (<=300s) challenge that every high-risk backup delete proof must sign over. While a challenge for the same (principal_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid the service returns the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new one. See key-management.md section 7.8.1.

High-risk delete guarded by a server-issued single-use challenge and the shared high-risk authority proof family (key-management.md section 7.8/7.8.1). The challenge is consumed atomically with the first successful delete; a byte-identical retry returns the stored terminal outcome, and the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

Transaction-bound monotonic erasure of the exact old secret_storage and mls_history series reserved by a SecurityRotationTransaction. Partial outcomes persist per series/object; exact retry never resurrects or rewrites an erased item. A complete outcome carries the sole canonical erase confirmation.

Requester-signed self KeyPackage claim. Exactly one holder_acceptance detached-JWS proof binds the complete proof-free request, authority service DID, requester and at-least-128-bit claim_nonce. The authority atomically commits KeyPackage CAS, (requester, claim_nonce, payload_digest) ledger and byte-identical terminal outcome; exact retries return that outcome and conflicting digest reuse fails before inventory lookup.

Closed selector XOR. current_admission binds the actual operation, request digest, verifier, audience and challenge and may authorize first live Signal evidence through current shared context. historical_event binds Event id, digest and receiver service and returns only the destination-signed admission receipt persisted when that exact Event was accepted; current state never reconstructs historical validity.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The closed Ed25519 proof binds the local key to the authoritative pairing handle, at-least-128-bit pairing secret, authority service DID, stable runtime binding and no-more-than-five-minute window; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize bound to the current proof digest. Pairing secret and proof MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 digest: same-binding retries retain approval/notification ids and atomically replace the current freshness proof, while a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key and treat a mismatch as paired-by-another-runtime. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). The new device submits a canonical new_device_pubkey and a client_nonce (plus optional display_name / device_metadata) and MUST NOT submit a challenge proof, because the proof must commit to values this call mints; the service mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id, an 8-character Crockford-style 40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code, a gate_audience and a server_nonce, and stores a bounded-TTL account-less record in state pending_authorization. The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it. Stage, resolve and status are rate limited. Each call mints a fresh request, so blind retries duplicate staged records: not retry-safe.

Resolves a device-pairing short-link token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the DevicePairingBootstrap. resolve MUST return a uniform not_found for unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a non-pending record so the failing condition is not enumerable. Authorization is unchanged: the returned bootstrap is only consumed by an authenticated device driving ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). While the record is open the outcome carries only state pending_authorization; once an authenticated device has authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus required device_id and authorized_event_ref; an expired record reports only state expired during a bounded cleanup retention period and becomes not_found after deletion.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.
Canonical HTTP binding is POST /_arkret/self/policy/check. Paths carry no version segment; protocol version is negotiated via *.describe / supported_operations (see sync/api-conventions.md).
Lists typed cross-Realm links projected from ak.realm.link. direction is outbound/inbound/both; link_kind_allow is a comma-separated allowlist of canonical link kinds.

Builds an ak.realm.link Control Move from realm_id -> target_realm_id. General directed cycles are valid and traversal uses a visited set; admission rejects only self-reference, invalid kind, invalid payload, or an illegal FSM transition. Self-reference returns schema_violation with reason_code realm_link_self_reference; an illegal transition returns failed_precondition with reason_code realm_link_invalid_transition.

Writes a tombstoning ak.realm.link Move (status=tombstoned) for the (realm_id, target_realm_id, link_kind) triple. link_kind defaults to governed_by; callers may override via the link_kind query param.

Returns the merged effective policy after walking governed_by / inherits_policy_from ancestors per the Realm's ak.realm.inheritance_policy. inheritance_mode=none when no inheritance policy is projected (implicit inheritance is forbidden).

Returns the projected ak.realm.organization relationship statements for the Realm (active / revoked / expired, latest-per-(organization_id, relationship)) plus declared owning_organizations hints with no verified statement. The caller must be authorized to read the Realm. A relationship is only verified when lifecycle_phase=verified_active; declared_organization_hints are unverified claims and MUST NOT be rendered as official / governed / endorsed.
Reads the projected ak.realm.policy_server config. Returns not_found when neither the Realm nor its governed_by ancestor chain declared one. from_org_fallback=true marks an inherited config.

Builds a durable ak.realm.policy_server Move whose payload is the closed request body (admission capability ak.policy.manage). Reducer validates the DID, canonical HTTPS policy-check URL and on_timeout enum. When the direct cell already has a settled declaration or tombstone, the Move MUST carry head_eq for that complete value; an absent direct cell is the only initial write.

After ak.policy.manage admission, a settled direct declaration is deleted by a durable ak.realm.policy_server Move with the exact payload {"tombstone":true} and head_eq for the complete declaration. The registered cas_register effect sets that value in the per-Realm cell; effective reads then ignore the direct binding and resume governed_by fallback or local-only capability evaluation. Repeating DELETE against a settled tombstone is an idempotent empty success and MUST NOT change the cell or state_root. A never-written or inherited-only direct cell returns not_found and MUST NOT mutate an ancestor.
Reads the Realm lifecycle projection (owner + members + deleted). Returns not_found when the Realm is invisible to the caller.

Builds a ak.realm.archive Move. The archived facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; archived=false clears the archived facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a ak.realm.freeze Move. The frozen facet changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; frozen=true rejects ordinary non-exempt writes with realm_frozen and frozen=false clears the freeze facet unless a terminal lifecycle state already applies.

Builds a terminal ak.realm.tombstone Move with a successor_realm_id. The tombstoned state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Builds a terminal ak.realm.destroy Move. The destroyed state changes when the lifecycle event is accepted into the Realm event log; later ordinary writes fail with realm_terminal_state.
Full event-log + operation dump for a Realm (schema ak.export.realm.v1). Caller must be authorized to read the Realm; payload visibility still follows Realm policy.
Returns the organization-inherited effective moderation policy view: inheritance chain, organization policy layers, the Realm's own override, and merged effective rules.

Writes a Realm moderation-policy override (ak.realm.moderation_policy). Only the Realm owner may write; an override that loosens an action an organization policy denies requires explicit organization approval embedded in the document, otherwise the server returns failed_precondition with reason_code=requires_organization_approval.

Candidate-profile private application intake. The applicant-signed receipt binds the accepted knock, policy/revision/private-body digests and applicant DID. The receipt and private body commit atomically and never enter shared Realm history.

Candidate-profile private reviewer decision. The reviewer-signed receipt binds the exact application revision and a capability grant/frontier proof; stale, expired or unauthorized decisions fail closed.
Candidate-profile private applicant cancellation. The caller and detached receipt signer must both be the original applicant.
Lists candidate application metadata. Reviewers and each matching applicant receive the protected body; other Realm members receive only application_pending placeholders.
Reads one candidate application for its applicant or an eligible reviewer. Every successful private-body read emits ak.audit.accessed.
Reads only the profile-private submit/read/review/cancel/invite-consume audit trail for one application. Applicant, eligible reviewer, or explicitly authorized Realm auditor only.
Lists holder-private consent cells for the authenticated holder only. Peer actors MUST NOT receive cell state, dots, expiry or request timestamps.
Reads one holder-private consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST equal holder_did or be an explicitly authorised holder controller; peers never receive this DTO.
Builds a ak.consent.grant Control Move on the holder's consent cell. The authenticated actor MUST be authorized to write the holder's consent (holder or an explicitly authorized controller/agent).

Builds a ak.consent.revoke Control Move enumerating the active grant dots for the (consent_id, peer, consent_scope). Revoking consent_scope=any cascades all concrete scopes; revoking a concrete scope leaves others intact.

Submits an opaque consent-contact request from the authenticated peer. peer_did defaults to and MUST equal the actor. The response is identical for missing holders, policy denial, rate limiting, silent drop and quarantine acceptance; the operation never returns a consent cell.
Lists the authenticated actor's account_data entries. content is stored verbatim and is opaque to the server.

Reads one account_data entry by account_data_key key, including its compare-and-set revision. Returns not_found when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; the not_found error.details carry account_data_cas_conflict_details so the caller still learns current_revision.

Builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write as a compare-and-set whole-value replacement: expected_revision must equal the accepted revision (0 to create) and the stored revision becomes expected_revision + 1. A mismatch returns cas_conflict with account_data_cas_conflict_details and stores nothing, so a stale offline retry can never overwrite a newer write. Controller-private registered types reject agent / applet / service principals. content is stored verbatim; clients own canonical encoding and (for sensitive keys) client-side encryption.

Stores a versioned tombstone for one account_data entry and fans out an actor-private update to the holder's other devices. The query parameter expected_revision is the same compare-and-set precondition as resource.replace; a mismatch returns cas_conflict and deletes nothing. The per-key revision high-water mark survives tombstone garbage collection, so a stale offline write can never resurrect the value. Key patterns whose deletion_mode is value_tombstone MUST NOT use this operation.

Builds a ak.read_cursor.advance actor-private write for (actor_id, realm_id, read_scope, position). Multi-device convergence is causal-first per zh/discovery/read-receipts.md section 6.5: a position that causally dominates the other wins regardless of HLC; HLC max applies only to causally concurrent positions, and device_id lexicographic order only breaks equal HLCs. The cursor is never published into shared Realm history.
Lists the authenticated actor's read markers, optionally filtered by the realm_id query param.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Strand lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Morph lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.
Extension read surface listing reducer-maintained Space lifecycle rows for a Realm. This is a derived read model, not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface that materializes a View{kind=collection} projection such as board/list/table/calendar. The response is a derived read model computed from signed Events, reducer profile, View definition, and the returned frontier; it is not a canonical truth source.

Optional extension read surface returning the authorized document body, version, relation, comment, and cursor-presence read-model for a single document Morph addressed within its Realm. Canonical truth remains the Morph/Relation/Message event history.

Holder-bound one-shot read of the current principal account projection. Returns principal_id, account lifecycle state, device summaries, optional ActorProfile, and signed handle-claim evidence or refs. It MUST NOT return an unsigned bare handle as authoritative identity. Naming: the trailing segment 'viewer' is intentionally outside the api-conventions.md §2.4 read-verb taxonomy; it follows the GraphQL 'viewer' convention (the authenticated subject's own projection). The target is located by the holder-bound session rather than an external id, so 'get' does not apply, and 'viewer' (subject identity projection) stays distinct from 'describe' (service capability metadata).

Holder-bound service wrapper around ak.profile.update / Actor Profile projection. Request body is a closed patch over display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>; profile_fields.bio is the canonical personal bio field and avatar_url is not accepted on the Arkret protocol path.

Streaming push of cross-Realm account-aggregate deltas (cross-Realm frontier, to_device queue, account_data, device_lists, unread / notification counts). Signal envelopes use the Signal Extension live rail and are not account aggregate state. Connection is long-lived; server pushes NDJSON frames as new data becomes available.

High-assurance optional endpoint to revoke a previously issued cursor authority. Revocation hits return cursor_revoked and MUST NOT advance account subscribe position, barrier wait, or dropped recovery state. To-device queue deletion is decoupled from cursors entirely and happens only via ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.
